theses.subject: Silver Miners
theses.thesis: Silver Miners is eligible, rank 2, with the strongest breadth in the top tier (breadth 1.0 vs 0.0 for Memory) and a higher durability bar (0.79 vs 0.44), suggesting more constituents are contributing to the trend rather than a single-name spike. theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners is the only top-tier theme with a clean 'trend' hurst tag, plus full breadth (1.0) and the highest durability bar in the top 5 (0.84). The trend discipline leg is the strongest here; crowding is not flagged. This is a trend-consistency lean on a theme the gate currently deems eligible.
theses.dissent: Gold miners are highly correlated with Silver Miners — this is effectively the same macro trade (precious metals) expressed two ways. A single precious-metals unwind would hit both. The trend tag is coincident, not predictive.

theses.subject: Memory, HBM & Storage
theses.thesis: The dominant theme (rank 1, score 3.05) sits on the absolute-trend gate (eligible) and is not crowded — but its breadth is 0.0 (single-name leadership, likely the HBM pure-play) and hurst is 'mixed'. This is a capped, trend-gate-lean on the leader: direction with the tape while it holds the gate, with no claim of rank-driven alpha. The guardrail explicitly forbids fading, so the honest expression of leadership is a modest overweight contingent on the gate holding.
theses.dissent: Breadth 0.0 means one name carries the theme — a single-stock shock would transmit directly to SMH (proxy). The headline weighting (0.25) is by far the largest, so SMH is effectively this theme plus three other semiconductor themes all sharing the same proxy; any semiconductor-wide selloff hits all four simultaneously.
